source: OpenCode ctx.tool.list() for the metaview server, signed in to a Metaview account; names and input schemas only

prompt.description: Instructions for what to extract from each conversation transcript (e.g. "Extract the candidate's salary expectations"). Automatically assessed and improved before creation unless skip_improvement=true.

value_type.description: Data type of the extracted value. Prefer constrained outputs so results can be filtered and grouped: boolean for yes/no; number for scores/ratings (e.g. 1-5); list for multiple items (not comma-separated text); single_line_text for categories — constrain the prompt to a fixed value set (e.g. 'Respond with exactly one of: None, Low, Moderate, High'), never free-form text with explanations. Use long_text only for genuinely open-ended answers.

field_id.description: Field ID of an existing AI field to update ('AI:<uuid>'); omit to create a new field. On update, changing the prompt, value_type, or name (for auto-prompted fields) CLEARS all existing results and triggers re-analysis on next query. System (prefab) fields cannot be updated.

skip_similarity_check.description: Create only. True skips the duplicate-field check and forces creation. Use when a previous call returned already_existed=true but the suggested field does not meet your needs. Default false.

skip_improvement.description: Create only. True skips the automatic prompt/value_type assessment and improvement, creating the field exactly as specified. Default false. Both what you submit and the improved version are compliance-checked; if the error says only the improved version was rejected, set this true to create your own wording as-is.

rationale.description: Always provide a brief explanation of why you are calling this tool

title.description: Name shown in the workspace's checks list.

prompt.description: Complete instructions for judging a job post.

check_type.description: Check category; list_job_post_checks returns category names and IDs.

rationale.description: Always provide a brief explanation of why you are calling this tool

filters.description: Filter objects ({field_id, operation, value}) defining which conversations the report covers. REQUIRED when creating (report_id omitted) — pass an empty list [] for all conversations. When updating, omit to leave filters unchanged. Filter value formats are data, not prose: list_fields returns a filter_formats map (operations + value_format per field type; a field's type key selects its entry). IMPORTANT: date filter values are a dict, not a bare date string. Example: {"field_id": "default:start_time", "operation": "after", "value": {"scope": "relative", "value": -2592000}}

report_id.description: UUID of an existing report to update. Omit to create a new report. On update, only the parameters you provide change.

name.description: Report name shown in the Reports list.

description.description: Optional report description, maximum 10 words. Omit or pass null to leave unchanged; pass an empty string to remove an existing description.

group.description: Field ID to group the report by (e.g. 'OSPT:<uuid>'; groupable=true in list_fields). Mutually exclusive with remove_grouping — never pass both.

remove_grouping.description: True: remove the report's existing grouping (update only). Mutually exclusive with group — never pass both.

field_ids.description: Field IDs (from list_fields) shown as the report's table columns.

sort_field.description: Field ID to sort conversation rows by (applied together with field_ids). Mutually exclusive with sort_metric, which sorts groups instead — never pass both.

sort_ascending.description: Sort direction for sort_field (default true = ascending).

metrics.description: Metrics computed per group on a grouped report. Each dict: metric_id (required, 'aggregation:...' or 'AI:<uuid>' from list_fields), function ('mean'|'median'|'sum'|'max'|'min'; default 'mean'), metric_arguments (optional dict — check required_arguments from list_fields). Defaults are applied when creating a grouped report without metrics.

sort_metric.description: How to sort groups on a grouped report: {metric_id, function ('mean'|'median'|'sum'|'max'|'min'), metric_arguments?} — same shape as metrics entries. Mutually exclusive with sort_field, which sorts conversation rows instead — never pass both.

sort_metric_ascending.description: Sort direction for sort_metric (default true = ascending).

only_show_recorded_conversations.description: True: the report covers only recorded conversations (creation default). False: also include unrecorded ones. Omit on update to leave unchanged.

expand_rows.description: Show grouped report rows expanded in the web-app UI.

min_group_conversation_count.description: Minimum conversations a group must have to appear in a grouped report.

candidates.description:
1-10 candidate lookups. Each is a dict with at least one identifier key — these exact keys and no others:
- candidate_id: Metaview candidate UUID (as returned by the application review, screening, and sourcing candidate tools).
- linkedin_url: LinkedIn profile URL ("https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-doe") or bare shorthand ("john-doe").
- email: candidate email address.
- phone_number: candidate phone number.
- participant_id: Metaview participant ID (e.g. from the default:candidate field in conversation data).
Optional scoped-access keys (each requires candidate_id and an accessible entity whose roster includes the candidate):
- application_review_id: Application Review UUID authorizing ATS access.
- screen_id: screen UUID authorizing ATS access.

chart_inputs.description: Chart specifications, each a dict with: metric_id (str, required) — 'aggregation:...' or 'AI:<uuid>' from list_fields. function (str) — one of Average, Median, Count, Sum, Max, Min, Cumulative, Rolling Average; must be in the metric's chart_functions. interval (str) — one of day, week, month, quarter. function and interval MUST be provided together (aggregate chart) or both omitted (scatter chart; the metric must have 'scatter' in chart_types). metric_arguments (dict, optional) — check required_arguments from list_fields. For contact-scoped metrics (question_count, talk_time, minutes_late) you MUST pass {"scope": "internal"} or {"scope": "external"}. "internal" = interviewers/hiring team, "external" = non-team participants (candidates, clients, etc.). function_arguments (dict, optional) — for Rolling Average pass {"windowIntervalCount": <int>}.

action.description: The operation to perform: create, update, delete, or set_rules.

sections.description:
Ordered list of section objects (list order = display order; max 100). Required when action=create; optional for update. FULL REPLACE on update: the list replaces ALL existing sections — omitted sections are removed. Include a section's existing id to update it in place; omit id for new sections.
Section shape (every field required):
  directive: 'SINGLE' (one block under a fixed heading) | 'REPEATING' (one block per detected entity — prefer this whenever the intent is 'one block per X', instead of several near-identical SINGLE sections)
  heading: str — required when directive='SINGLE'
  repeating_entity: str — required when directive='REPEATING' (e.g. 'Question', 'Topic', 'Role', 'Project')
  description: str — THE most important field: a PROMPT run on every transcript, not a note to a human. Cover (a) SCOPE — what to include and leave out — and (b) OUTPUT FORMAT — length caps, markdown patterns, label conventions (e.g. '3 bullets max, each **Label:** one sentence, under 120 words'). REPEATING descriptions run once per detected entity.
  output: dict, one of:
    {'type': 'TEXT', 'text_format': 'PARAGRAPH'|'BULLET_POINT', 'detail': 'low'|'medium'|'high'} — use TEXT for anything that isn't a hard classification; carry structure via markdown in the description.
    {'type': 'NUMBER', 'currency': str} — '' for a plain number, else 'USD', 'EUR', ...
    {'type': 'OPTIONS', 'options_type': 'SINGLE'|'MULTIPLE', 'options': [str, ...]} — the description MUST give per-option selection criteria (exactly when to pick each value and when NOT to); for booleans use options=['true', 'false'] with options_type='SINGLE'.
    {'type': 'DATE', 'date_format': str, e.g. 'yyyy/mm/dd'|'mm/dd/yyyy'|'dd/mm/yyyy'}

group_name.description: update only. Move the template into a named accessible folder; pass '' or 'personal' for the personal folder. Resolve folder names via list_note_template_groups first. Omit to leave the template where it is.

filters.description: Required for set_rules only. Full replacement of When to Use conditions, combined with AND. Pass [] to disable automatic selection for the chosen scope. Each object has field_id, operation, and value. Discover field IDs/operations with list_fields and values with list_field_values. Filter value formats are data, not prose: list_fields returns a filter_formats map (operations + value_format per field type; a field's type key selects its entry). IMPORTANT: date filter values are a dict, not a bare date string. Example: {"field_id": "default:start_time", "operation": "after", "value": {"scope": "relative", "value": -2592000}}

apply_to_workspace.description: set_rules only. False (default): personal rules. True: admin-only workspace rules, replacing everyone's personal copies; $self is not allowed. An admin saving personal rules also disables workspace rules for this template. Rules affect future automatic selection; existing notes are not regenerated.

action.description: The operation to perform: create, update, duplicate, or delete.

sequence_id.description: Sequence UUID. Required when action=update, duplicate, or delete.

name.description: Sequence name. Required when action=create; optional for update (renames).

description.description: Sequence description. Optional for create and update.

set_enabled.description: Enable or disable the sequence. Optional for create and update.

unsendable_step_behavior.description: What the sequence's AUTOMATIC steps do when they can't reach the candidate (no email, phone number or LinkedIn profile for the step's channel, WhatsApp rejects the number, or the email bounces): PAUSE_SEQUENCE pauses the candidate's sequence until someone fixes it; SKIP_STEP skips that step and the sequence carries on. Manual steps always pause. Optional for create and update.

steps.description:
FULL REPLACE (update action only): this list replaces the sequence's current steps — steps not in the list are DELETED. Each step's schedule is required (schedule_type values: instant, later, next_business_day; specific_time is rejected). time_of_day accepts 'HH:MM' or 'HH:MM:SS'.
    steps: Optional for update. A JSON list of step objects to replace the current steps.
        Steps not in the list are deleted. Order in the list determines step order.
        Each step object has:
            channel_type: str (REQUIRED — one of: EMAIL, LINKEDIN_CONNECTION, LINKEDIN_INMAIL, LINKEDIN_MESSAGE, SMS, PHONE, WHATSAPP)
            sequence_step_id: str | null (include the existing step ID to update it;
                omit or set null for new steps — an ID will be generated automatically)
            template: str | null (message body; supports {{variable_name}} placeholders
                that are filled in per-candidate by an AI call before sending)
            description: str | null
            schedule: dict | null (e.g. {"schedule_type": "instant"}, {"schedule_type": "later", "delay_seconds": 86400}, {"schedule_type": "next_business_day", "time_of_day": "09:00:00"}.
                Setting a specific time is NOT supported.
            step_execution_type: str | null (AUTOMATIC or MANUAL)
            execution_timeout_seconds: int | null (only for MANUAL steps)

        EMAIL step fields:
            from_mailbox_id: REQUIRED (mailbox UUID — use list_mailboxes to get available mailboxes)
            step_type: REQUIRED (NEW_THREAD or REPLY)
            bcc: optional (list of email addresses)
            cc: optional (list of email addresses)
            step_execution_type: AUTOMATIC, MANUAL (default: AUTOMATIC)
            NOT used: from_whatsapp_account_id, linkedin_subject
            step_type values: NEW_THREAD or REPLY
            subject: str | null (REQUIRED for NEW_THREAD; forbidden for REPLY. Supports {{variable_name}} placeholders)

        LINKEDIN_CONNECTION step fields:
            step_execution_type: MANUAL (default: MANUAL)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, from_whatsapp_account_id, linkedin_subject, step_type
            Connection request with optional note; recommended maximum 275 characters including resolved placeholders (stored in template field)

        LINKEDIN_INMAIL step fields:
            linkedin_subject: REQUIRED (str — required subject line for the InMail)
            step_execution_type: MANUAL (default: MANUAL)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, from_whatsapp_account_id, step_type
            InMail to non-connections. Requires subject + body. Uses Premium LinkedIn credits.

        LINKEDIN_MESSAGE step fields:
            linkedin_subject: optional (str | null — subject line for the LinkedIn message)
            step_execution_type: MANUAL (default: MANUAL)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, from_whatsapp_account_id, step_type
            subject shorthand: setting 'subject' auto-maps to linkedin_subject

        SMS step fields:
            step_execution_type: MANUAL (default: MANUAL)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, from_whatsapp_account_id, linkedin_subject, step_type

        PHONE step fields:
            step_execution_type: MANUAL (default: MANUAL)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, from_whatsapp_account_id, linkedin_subject, step_type

        WHATSAPP step fields:
            from_whatsapp_account_id: optional (ignored; the connected sender is selected automatically)
            step_execution_type: AUTOMATIC, MANUAL (default: AUTOMATIC)
            NOT used: bcc, cc, from_mailbox_id, linkedin_subject, step_type
            Automatic steps use the step creator's connected WhatsApp account.

sections.description: The complete, final interview plan as a list of section objects — the same shape get_screen_details returns in interview_plan.sections. FULL REPLACE: this replaces the current plan wholesale, and sections/questions not in the list are deleted — never send a diff or partial edit. Each section: {section_id, title, goal?, questions}. Each question: {question_id, prompt, kind?, options?, follow_up?, rubric?, output_type?, multi_select?, candidate_role?, character?}. kind is exactly one of 'conversational' (asked out loud), 'multiple_choice' (options required; options and multi_select apply only to this kind — multi_select true lets the candidate pick several options), 'slack_thread' (answered in writing), or 'role_play' (a spoken scene the interviewer plays in character; candidate_role is who the candidate is in the scene and character is the interviewer's private brief for who they play — both apply only to this kind). output_type is 'FIT', 'BOOLEAN', 'NUMBER', 'SHORT_TEXT', or 'DATE'. Keep the ids of nodes you carry over — kind, output_type, multi_select, and question history follow the id, and omitted fields are preserved from the current node; invent new unique ids for new nodes (defaults: conversational, FIT). Omit this parameter entirely to keep the current sections and update only the context fields (once candidates are invited, a context-only update still makes a new version).
